title: Stroke-like symptoms
reference: NASA ISS Medical Operations: Acute Neurological Deficit Protocol & Cincinnati / F.A.S.T. Assessment Standards.

q1.text: F (Face): Ask astronaut to smile. Is there unilateral facial droop, mouth asymmetry, or loss of nasolabial fold?

q2.text: A (Arms): Ask astronaut to close eyes and hold both arms extended forward in microgravity. Does one arm drift downward or show sudden weakness or numbness?

q3.text: S (Speech): Ask astronaut to repeat 'The sky is blue and clear.' Is speech slurred, garbled, or are they unable to comprehend or articulate?

q4.text: Does the astronaut experience sudden severe 'thunderclap' headache, diplopia (double vision), or acute loss of limb coordination (ataxia)?

i_stroke_time.text: T (Time): Note exact Zulu time of onset. Position astronaut with head elevated 30 degrees. Check capillary blood glucose immediately to rule out acute hypoglycemia mimic, and maintain O2 saturation >= 96%.

end_monitor.text: F.A.S.T. neurological screen negative. No focal deficits observed. Conduct cranial nerve screening and monitor for 6 hours.

end_escalate.text: CRITICAL ACUTE NEUROLOGICAL EMERGENCY: Immediate Flight Surgeon consultation active. Prepare telemedicine video link and emergency Neuro-ICU kit.
